sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 of the Hudson County volume 8 series, titled Weehawken and West New York and drawn at 150 feet to an inch, covers the West Shore Railroad terminals on the Hudson River waterfront below the Palisades, from the ferry and passenger station at the foot of Clifton Road north past the West New York boundary line to the grain elevators at Pier 8. Hudson Boulevard East runs down the left side along the top of the cliff, with only the ends of the side streets drawn, from 10th Street in West New York south through 7th to 2nd Streets and Fulton Street, Columbia Terrace and Clifton Terrace in Weehawken; the area west of the boulevard is marked as shown in Volume Eight. Clifton Road descends from the boulevard to the waterfront and ends at an iron bridge and trolley trestle. Below the cliff the sheet is filled by the yard tracks of the West Shore Railroad (New York Central and Hudson River Railroad), the tunnel entrances, a repair yard, an ice house, a round house and turntable, the fruit transfer and passenger yards with their sheds, the passenger station with the National and Northern Pacific express offices, transfer bridge slips 1 to 4 and ferry slips 1 to 6 for the 42nd Street and Desbrosses Street ferries. Piers 1 to 8 extend into the river, with iron-clad freight houses on piers 2, 3 and 4, two proposed piers, the West Shore elevator (new) and the West Shore grain elevator, each with a note on its fire protection. A general report on the terminals' fire brigade and water supply is printed at lower left, and the pier and bulkhead lines approved by the Secretary of War in 1897 are drawn in the river.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East is now Boulevard East.

The numbered streets on the boulevard are now 46th Street (2nd), 47th Street (3rd), 48th Street (4th) and 49th Street (5th), identified from the block spacing and confirmed by the fit; 6th, 7th and 10th Streets were not matched.
The West Shore terminal, piers and ferry slips have been replaced by the Port Imperial development; no railroad feature was used as control.
Drawn at 150 ft to an inch, three times smaller than the 50 ft sheets.

Weehawken & West New York, West Shore R.R. terminals, piers 1-8 and ferry slips; Hudson Boulevard East with old West New York numbered streets, Fulton St, Columbia Ter, Clifton Ter, Clifton Rd. Scale 150 ft to an inch. From the Volume 8 series (sheet 29).

sheet-51.description: Sheet 51 of the Hudson County volume 8 series shows the Hackensack Water Company's Reservoir No. 2 and the streets around it on the upland of Weehawken, at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Palisade Avenue runs along the top of the sheet with a dash-dot line down its middle marking the boundary between West Hoboken and Weehawken, and Highpoint Avenue forms the right edge, partly cut off by the sheet margin. Washington runs down the left side on a slant along the same town line, and Gregory Avenue closes the bottom. The reservoir, block 14, fills nearly the whole sheet: a rounded rectangular basin with a pale blue embankment and the legend of the water company and its reservoir number, with a small gate house at its east side where large water mains of 20, 24 and 30 inches cross Highpoint Avenue. Beneath it a row of narrow lots fronts on Gregory Avenue; two small frame dwellings there are marked 'To be built' and 'Being built'. A fire alarm box and hydrant stand on Gregory Avenue and water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are drawn in the streets. At the top two West Hoboken streets, Stevens and Monastery, are lettered where they meet Palisade Avenue. The margins carry the numbers of the neighbouring sheets, 30, 5, 6 and 58, and Mountain Road is lettered at the lower left corner.
notes: Stevens Street and Monastery Street run into Palisade Avenue on the West Hoboken (Union City) side; by distance along Palisade Avenue from Highpoint Avenue they correspond to today's 20th Street and 21st Street.
Washington is not matched in the modern street data (probably Manhattan Avenue or an unnamed way); it was not used for control.

Hackensack Water Co reservoir No. 2 block between Palisade Av, Highpoint Av, Gregory Av and Washington (Weehawken / West Hoboken line). 50 ft. 1 detected + 2 hand-picked junctions at the edges (Mountain Rd uncertain); low confidence.

sheet-52.description: Sheet 52 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers a residential section of upland Weehawken at the West Hoboken line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. The sheet is bounded by Palisade Avenue along the top, where a dash-dot line marks the boundary between West Hoboken and Weehawken down the middle of the street, and by Gregory Avenue along the bottom; Highpoint Avenue runs along the left edge and Dodd Street along the right. Oak Street and Shippen Street run between them, and Hudson Avenue crosses the sheet at mid-height, giving six numbered blocks (17 to 21 and the part of block 20 south of Hudson Avenue). The blocks are lined with narrow house lots, most of them built up with two- and two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings, with brick rows of three-storey flats and a block of brick flats with a ground-floor insurance office at the corner of Palisade Avenue and Dodd Street. House numbers are given along every frontage. Water pipes of 6, 20, 24 and 30 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and a fire alarm box at Highpoint and Hudson Avenues and at Shippen Street. The lower right of the sheet, south of Hudson Avenue and east of Shippen Street, is left blank and carries the number of sheet 54, which draws it; the margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 29, 51, 53, 57 and 58, and the area beyond Palisade Avenue lies in West Hoboken, outside the volume.
notes: West Hoboken is now part of Union City; Palisade Avenue still marks the Weehawken line.
Oak, Shippen and Dodd are printed without a suffix; today they are Oak Street, Shippen Street and Dodd Street.
Palisade Av to Gregory Av, Highpoint Av to Dodd St (Oak, Shippen, Hudson Av). 50 ft. Pilot.

sheet-53.description: Sheet 53 covers a block-sized stretch of upland Weehawken between Palisade Avenue on the west, along the West Hoboken line, and Hudson Avenue on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Palisade Avenue runs up the page. At the top the Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) crosses diagonally with the boundary line of the Town of Union marked along its north side, and a triangular block between the plank road, Maple and Palisade Avenue is occupied by coal yards, a garage, flats, and the Bodenmann Manufacturing Company embroidery works with a large mill building and a tin smith's shop. Below Maple stands Public School No. 2, a large brick building with a connected annex, and frame houses with a bakery and an insurance office on Palisade Avenue. South of Angelique the blocks are laid out in regular rows of narrow lots: block 27 between Angelique and Jane, and block 23 between Jane and Dodd, nearly all two-storey dwellings and flats with house numbers on each frontage, and a row of shops including a drug store at the corner of Dodd. Water mains of 4, 6 and 24 inches are drawn in the streets, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes. Neighbouring sheet numbers 35, 32, 31, 29, 54 and 52 are lettered in the margins.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is the modern Hackensack Avenue and Plank Road.
Elm Street and the left-hand Maple Street are West Hoboken streets drawn outside the Weehawken line.
Maple, Angelique, Jane and Dodd are printed without a suffix; today they are Maple Street, Angelique Street, Jane Street and Dodd Street.
Dodd St to Hackensack Plank Road, Jane, Maple, Angelique, Palisade Av (vertical, West Hoboken line). 50 ft, turned (rotation -25).

sheet-54.description: Sheet 54 shows the upland district of Weehawken lying between Hudson Avenue and Gregory Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 25 degrees. The Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) crosses the upper part from upper left to lower right along the line of the Town of Union boundary, and Maple, Ridgeley Place and Pleasant Avenue branch from it. In the north part, blocks 31 and 32 are lined with narrow lots, mostly two- and three-storey dwellings and flats, with a few stores. South of Maple, block 28 holds the Palm, Flechterer and Company decalcomanie works, a large brick factory, and several embroidery factories. In the lower half block 25 is dominated by a large range of glass greenhouses, with the Tipless Lamp Company and the Enterprise Embroidery Works beside them, and the lots of blocks 24 and 22 along Dodd and Shippen are lined with two-storey dwellings. A well tower and a Palisade Hose Company house stand on Jane Street. Fire alarm boxes, hydrants and water pipes are drawn throughout. Blocks to the left (53, 52) and right (59, 57) and above (32) are numbers of the adjoining sheets.
notes: Ridgeley Place and Maple still exist as Ridgeley Place and Maple Street.
Jane, Dodd and Shippen are printed without a suffix; today they are Jane Street, Dodd Street and Shippen Street.
The Plank Road junctions with Hudson Avenue, Gregory Avenue and Pleasant Avenue were not detected and were not used for control.
Hackensack Plank Road, Ridgeley Pl, Maple, Jane, Dodd, Shippen, Gregory Av, Hudson Av. 50 ft, turned (rotation -26).

sheet-55.description: Sheet 55 shows a hilly corner of Weehawken along the line with West Hoboken and Hoboken at the head of the Hackensack Plank Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 90 degrees from the sheets to the east, so that West 19th Street runs down the right side and Grand Street crosses the middle. The boundary of Weehawken is marked by dashed lines along the left and right edges. The sheet is mostly built up with dwellings and flats in narrow lots, with brick flats and stores on Grand Street and West 19th Street, a plumber, a drug store and saloons on the corners, Public School No. 2 with a connected annex, a club, a cooper shop, and a coal yard and a block of buildings east of Chestnut. At the bottom the Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) crosses diagonally, with St. Lawrence Roman Catholic Church and School on Clinton Street, small flats, Lehigh coal yard and sheds near Clinton, and the triangular blocks 6 and 7 below the road. A fire alarm box stands at Grand Street and another at the foot of West 19th Street. The upper part is a block of long narrow lots labelled 1, beyond the West Hoboken line, which is outside the sheet. The words 'See Volume Seven' lie in the left margin, where the map continues in another volume.
notes: Chestnut, Grand and Clinton are printed without a suffix; today they are Chestnut Street, Grand Street and Clinton Street.
West 18th Street was not used for control: its drawn centre line lies about 5 m from the modern 18th Street.
The sheet is turned about 90 degrees from the sheets to the east (fitted rotation 87 degrees).

W. 19th St, W. 18th St, Chestnut, Grand, Clinton, Hackensack Plank Road (West Hoboken / Hoboken lines). 50 ft, turned 90 degrees (rotation 87). 3 detected + 1 hand-picked; W. 18th St left out (about 5 m from the modern 18th Street).

sheet-56.description: Sheet 56 covers the foot of the Palisades slope in central Weehawken, from the Hackensack Plank Road on the west to the railway yards on the east, drawn at 50 feet to an inch. The plank road (Turnpike) and Branch Road run up the page, with West 19th Street, 19th Street and 18th Street crossing them, and Hudson Boulevard East (Park Avenue) forms the wide street through the east side. On the west side the blocks between the plank road and Willow Avenue hold Baldwin Hose Company No. 1, St. Lawrence Roman Catholic Church and School, a bakery, saloons and rows of two- and three-storey dwellings, and below them the Lehigh Coal and Supply Company yard. East of Branch Road stand Public School No. 1 and many houses, and on the east side of Willow Avenue the Hobbs, Benton and Heath wall paper factory and the Weehawken Contracting Company electric light plant, sewage disposal plant and lamp works, all in large brick buildings. Along Hudson Boulevard East are McCann and Callery's coal pockets and the Erie Railroad freight depot, with the tracks of the New Jersey Junction and Erie railroads and a viaduct approach across the east side. A chicken house stands in the top right corner. Block numbers 34, 35, 58, 69 and 55 mark the neighbouring sheets.
notes: Hudson B'l'v'd East is the modern Boulevard East; the sheet gives (Park Av.) beneath its name.
Branch Road does not appear in the modern street data and Park Avenue has two parallel ways in it; junctions on Park Avenue sit 3 to 5 m off in the fit.
Clinton is printed without a suffix; today it is Clinton Street.
Willow Avenue, Branch Road and the area east of them were rebuilt for the Lincoln Tunnel approaches; the fit to modern streets here is weak.

Hackensack Plank Road, Branch Road, 19th St, 18th St, Willow Av, Hudson Blvd East (Park Av), Paul's Row, Erie freight depot. 50 ft. 4 detected; Park Avenue has two modern carriageways here; medium-low confidence.

sheet-57.description: Sheet 57 shows the south edge of upland Weehawken where the Hackensack Plank Road swings south along the hillside, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about 25 degrees. Gregory Avenue runs down the left edge, with Shippen and Oak streets crossing it, and the plank road (Turnpike) follows a long curve across the centre with Branch Road and Hudson Boulevard East beyond it to the east. At the top left a large three-storey machine shop and embroidery factory stands in the triangle between Sunnyside Avenue and the plank road, with a brick block of flats beside it. West of the plank road the blocks (26, 22, 15) are mostly open, with scattered frame dwellings, an auto repair shop, a small junk shop, and a row of dwellings on Shippen Street; a house marked Villa Jane stands on Oak Street. A long row of lots on the east side of the plank road holds frame dwellings, a town hall, saloons, a horse shed and shops, and Shippen Street Steps climb the bluff between them. Baldwin Avenue (Coal Dock Road) curves in at the lower right across the large sweep of Hudson Boulevard East, and a compass rose is drawn at the upper right. Neighbouring block numbers 54, 52, 58, 59, 72, 70 and 35 appear in the margins.
notes: Shippen and Oak are printed without a suffix; today they are Shippen Street and Oak Street.
Baldwin Avenue is also lettered '(Coal Dock Road)'.
Gregory Avenue lies on the left edge of the sheet and the Hackensack Plank Road junctions were hand-picked; scale and rotation come out a few percent from the neighbouring sheets.

Gregory Av (Sunnyside Av at the top), Shippen, Oak, Hackensack Plank Road, Branch Road, Hudson Blvd East, Baldwin Av (Coal Dock Road). 50 ft. No junction detected; placed from Gregory/Shippen and Gregory/Oak carried from sheet 52 plus two hand-picked junctions on the plank road; block along Gregory drawn about 5 percent short. Low confidence.

sheet-58.description: Sheet 58 of the Hudson County volume 8 series shows the upland of Weehawken on the western side of the Hackensack Plank Road corridor, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left, the sheet turned so that Gregory Avenue runs down its left edge. Most of the left and centre of the sheet is a single tract of long, narrow lots running from Gregory Avenue across to Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), almost all of them empty; only a handful of frame and brick dwellings stand on the Gregory Avenue end and a few buildings on the Plank Road frontage. A covered tank of the Hackensack Water Company with its valve house stands at the top, inside a fenced lot with six-inch to thirty-inch water pipes running across the sheet. Hackensack Plank Road, Branch Road and Hudson Boulevard East run as three roughly parallel strips down the middle and right, converging at the bottom, where Hudson Boulevard East is lettered with Park Avenue in brackets. Where Branch Road ends a triangular block holds a saloon, a wood working shop of the Hudson Wood Working Company, a Presbyterian church and rows of dwellings and flats along Park Avenue. At the right a coal yard (Jagel and Bellis) and the Lang Brothers ice and produce yard with a wagon shed fill the east side. The Weehawken and West Hoboken boundary line crosses the lower left, with public steps running down the cliff at the bottom corner. The upper right and right are blank where sheet 69 draws the railroad yards.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East south of the fork is Park Avenue on the sheet; today it is Park Avenue, while the northern part is Boulevard East.
Hackensack Plank Road is now Hackensack Avenue and Plank Road.
Branch Road is not in the current street extract.
Mountain Road, at the lower left, is only partly on the sheet and its name was read from a cut-off label; medium confidence.
Placed from Gregory Avenue / Highpoint Avenue carried from sheet 52 and the corners of the Flats building on Paul's Row carried from sheet 56 (helmert); low to medium confidence.

Gregory Av, Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike), Branch Road, Hudson Blvd East (Park Av), Hackensack Water Co covered tank, Jagel & Bellis coal yard, 1st Presbyterian church. 50 ft. No drawn junction between surviving streets except Gregory / Highpoint at the edge: placed from 2 points carried from sheet 52 (Gregory / Highpoint) and 3 from sheet 56 (Flats building on Paul's Row); helmert, low-medium confidence.

sheet-59.description: Sheet 59 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers the upland of Weehawken along the Town of Union line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Pleasant Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet with the municipal boundary lettered Town of Union and Weehawken along it, and Hackensack Plank Road (Turnpike) runs diagonally from the upper left corner to meet it, with Ridgeley Place branching off near the corner. Kossuth Street and Cantelo Street enter from the north across the boundary. Sunnyside Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet, and Branch Road, a wide diagonal street, crosses from lower left to upper right; Hauxhurst Avenue, Gracie Place and Sterling Avenue are laid out on the right, where only lot lines and no buildings are drawn. Hudson Boulevard East curves across the bottom. The frontage on Pleasant Avenue, Hackensack Plank Road and Sunnyside Avenue is built up with frame dwellings, brick flats and two long rows of attached dwellings marked concrete, on both sides of Sunnyside Avenue; a saloon stands at the corner of Plank Road and Pleasant Avenue. The lower half of the sheet is open ground cut by Branch Road, with a few outlying houses. Water pipes are drawn in the streets with hydrants and a fire alarm box. The margins carry the numbers of sheets 32, 35, 37, 54, 57, 60 and 72, and a scale bar and compass rose appear at the bottom.
notes: Hackensack Plank Road is now Hackensack Avenue and Plank Road; Sunnyside Avenue is now Gregory Avenue.
Branch Road follows today's Park Avenue; Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East.
Cantelo Street is Cantello Street today.
Gracie Place and Kossuth Street were read from the overview and are medium confidence; Kossuth Street may be today's 33rd Street.

Placed from one point carried from sheet 60 (the corner west of Cantelo Street at Pleasant Avenue) with the scale and rotation of sheet 60; modern Pleasant Avenue junctions are spaced about 12 percent closer than the drawn ones, so they were not used.

Pleasant Av, Hackensack Plank Road, Branch Road, Hauxhurst Av, Sterling Av, Hudson Blvd East. 50 ft, north up-right (rotation 60). Anchored on one corner carried from sheet 60; modern Pleasant Av junctions spaced about 12 percent closer than drawn (Lincoln Tunnel area). Low confidence.

sheet-60.description: Sheet 60 of the Hudson County volume 8 series shows the upland of Weehawken between Bulls Ferry Road and Hudson Boulevard East, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Pleasant Avenue and Bulls Ferry Road cross the top of the sheet along the boundary with the Town of Union, with Cantelo Street, Weehawken Street and Franklin Street entering from the north; Jefferson Street runs down the right edge. Branch Road sweeps in from the left and curves into Hauxhurst Avenue, which runs across the middle of the sheet, and Denning Place and Sterling Avenue branch off below it. Hudson Boulevard East curves across the lower part of the sheet. The blocks between Bulls Ferry Road and Hauxhurst Avenue are lined with frame dwellings of two storeys and brick or frame flats, and a few larger dwellings and a stone house stand west of Denning Place. Much of the ground south of Hauxhurst Avenue is laid out in long lots with no buildings. The block at the right edge holds frame dwellings and a club house. At the bottom, houses stand on Bonn Place and High Bluff Terrace beside the numbers of sheets 62 and 72, which draw the adjoining ground. Water pipes of 6 inches and larger are drawn in the streets with hydrants and the lettered street widths of 40, 50 and 80 feet. A compass rose and scale bar fill the lower right.
notes: Bulls Ferry Road is Park Avenue today; the Weehawken and Union City line follows it.
Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East today; Cantelo Street is Cantello Street.
Jefferson is printed without a suffix; today it is Jefferson Street.
Branch Road is not in the current street extract; it was replaced by the Lincoln Tunnel approaches.
Weehawken Street may now be Peter Street; this is not certain.
The names Bonn Place, High Bluff Terrace and Bellevue Street at the foot of the sheet were read from the overview and are medium confidence.
Pleasant Av / Bulls Ferry Road at top, Hauxhurst, Denning Pl, Sterling, Jefferson, Hudson Blvd East, High Bluff Ter, Bonn Pl. 50 ft, north up-right (rotation 60). 4 detected.

sheet-61.description: Sheet 61 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers a thinly built part of upland Weehawken at the Town of Union line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right. Bulls Ferry Road crosses the upper part of the sheet from left to right, with a dash-dot boundary line along it at the left and another, lettered Town of Union and Weehawken, running to the right edge near Union Street. Hauxhurst Avenue runs across the middle of the sheet, Jefferson Street runs down the left side to Sterling Avenue, and Highwood Terrace runs diagonally down the right side with Edgar Street and Nesbit Street meeting it from the east. Hudson Boulevard East sweeps in a curve across the lower part, and Park View Avenue and Highwood Avenue appear at the bottom edge. The blocks carry a row of attached brick flats and dwellings in pink on Bulls Ferry Road, rows of detached frame dwellings on both sides of Hauxhurst Avenue, a few dwellings along Highwood Terrace and large undeveloped tracts of long lots between. Water pipes of 6, 12 and 16 inches are drawn in Bulls Ferry Road and Union Street, with hydrants. The lower middle of the sheet, between the boulevard and Park View Avenue, is almost empty except for one dwelling. The margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 34, 36, 60 and 63, and a compass rose stands at the upper left.
notes: Bulls Ferry Road is Park Avenue today, and the Weehawken line with Union City (the old Town of Union) runs along it.
Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East today; Park View Avenue is Parkview Avenue.
Jefferson is printed without a suffix; today it is Jefferson Street.
Blum Street was read from the overview and is low confidence; it is not a street in the current extract.
Bulls Ferry Road, Hauxhurst Av, Jefferson, Sterling, Highwood Ter, Edgar, Nesbit, Park View Av. 50 ft, north up-right (rotation 59).

sheet-62.description: Sheet 62 of the Hudson County volume 8 series shows a residential district of Weehawken on the eastern slope of the Palisades, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left. Hudson Boulevard East runs along the top of the sheet, curving at its left end where Highwood Avenue and Highwood Terrace join it, and the sheet lies between that boulevard and Bellevue Street near the bottom. Park View Avenue runs down the left side, Bonn Place and King Avenue run down the middle, and Hamilton Avenue crosses the right-hand part, with a second Hamilton Avenue running down the right edge. The blocks, numbered 41, 42, 43, 44 and others, are lined with detached frame dwellings of two and two-and-a-half storeys, most of them with porches and outbuildings, set on generous lots; two brick dwellings are shown pink on the right and a few flats and brick buildings on the left. Six-inch and larger water pipes are drawn in the streets with their sizes and hydrants, and street widths of 50 and 60 feet are lettered. The blocks west of Bonn Place are bounded by an irregular line along the slope, beyond which the paper is left blank. Below Bellevue Street the sheet shows the north side of a block of detached houses, with High Bluff Terrace meeting Bellevue at the bottom. The margins carry the numbers of the adjoining sheets 60, 61, 64, 71 and 72, and a compass rose and scale bar fill the lower right.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East is Boulevard East today.
Park View Avenue is Parkview Avenue today; Bellevue is Bellevue Street and Bellevue Terrace.
Bonn Place, King Avenue and Hamilton Avenue keep their names. Highwood Avenue and Highwood Terrace also survive.
The King Avenue and Bellevue Street junction carries a residual of about 3.6 m against the modern node.
Hudson Blvd East, Bonn Pl, King Av, Hamilton Av, Bellevue, High Bluff Ter, Park View Av. 50 ft, rotation -30. 2 detected + 2 hand-picked, all near the King Av column; medium confidence.

sheet-63.description: Sheet 63 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers the upland strip of Weehawken along Bulls Ferry Road, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north towards the upper left (the compass arrow, which is magnetic, points to the lower right of the sheet's own north). The Town of Union boundary line runs down Bulls Ferry Road on the left, and the streets of Union, lettered at the left margin, lie outside the Weehawken map. Most of the centre is taken by Reservoir No. 1 of the Hackensack Water Co., a walled basin with a gate house on its west side; at the upper left the company's works are drawn in pink, with its office, a water tower of 170 feet marked not in use, pumps marked not in use, a repair shop and a store house. Along the top, Highwood Avenue or Liberty Place carries a row of nine yellow frame dwellings and flats, and Highwood Avenue turns down the right side of the reservoir, lined with frame dwellings, two buildings marked cement blocks, a carpenter shop and a larger flat-roofed building. The lower third is block 39, bounded by Highwood Terrace along the bottom, with Edgar and Nesbit running up between rows of frame dwellings, a brick row of attached houses on Highwood Terrace, the Highwood Garage at the upper left of the block and a large brick building with an office at the lower left. Highwood Avenue curves out of the sheet at the lower right towards Park View Avenue and Hudson Boulevard East. The area to the right of Highwood Avenue is left blank and carries the numbers of sheets 65 and 64, and sheet 61 lies below Highwood Terrace. Water pipes of 6, 12, 16, 20 and 30 inches, hydrants and fire alarm boxes are shown in the streets.
notes: Edgar and Nesbit are printed without a suffix; today they are Edgar Street and Nesbit Street. Highwood Ter. is now Highwood Terrace, Park View Av. is now Parkview Avenue and Hudson Blvd. East is now Boulevard East.
Highwood Avenue or Liberty Place along the top is Liberty Place on modern maps.
Bulls Ferry Road along the left is Park Avenue on modern maps (the sheet's neighbours were fitted to it under that name).
Control points are few: 5 detected junctions along Highwood Terrace and Highwood Avenue and one hand-picked at Highwood Avenue and Hudson Place; the reservoir area has none.
Highwood Av / Liberty Pl, Hackensack Water Co reservoir No. 1, Highwood Ter, Edgar, Nesbit. 50 ft, rotation -20.

sheet-64.description: Sheet 64 of the Hudson County volume 8 series shows a residential district of upland Weehawken on the cliff edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the right and slightly upward. The sheet is bounded at the top by Highwood Avenue, which crosses the upper part on a long diagonal and bends at the upper left, and at the bottom by Hudson Boulevard East, which curves round the lower left corner and runs along the foot of the blocks. Three streets run down between them, Duer Place, Hudson Place and Eldorado Place, dividing the area into blocks 47, 48 and 49; the short street across the top of block 47, lettered Park View Avenue or Duer Place, joins Duer Place to the boulevard at the left. The blocks are laid out in narrow lots, most of them with detached two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings in yellow, a few brick or tile-walled houses in pink, small garages and an automobile building, and some upper lots left empty where the lots reach back to Highwood Avenue. The Highwood Fire Engine Co. house, with a hose tower, stands on the curve of Highwood Avenue at the head of Duer Place. A 6 inch water pipe runs in each street, with hydrants and fire alarm boxes at several corners. The blank areas at the top, left and right belong to other sheets, whose numbers (63, 62, 65, 66) are printed there, and the estate below the boulevard is carried on sheet 71. The compass in the upper left points to magnetic north.
notes: Hudson B'l'v'd East is now Boulevard East; Park View Av. or Duer Pl. is now Parkview Avenue at its upper end and Duer Place below.
Only four junctions are used for control (Duer Place and Hudson Place at the boulevard, Hudson Place and Eldorado Place at Highwood Avenue); the fit has no leave-one-out figure.
The curved stretch of the boulevard at the lower left and the five-way junction at the left edge were not used as control.
Highwood Av, Park View Av or Duer Pl, Duer Pl, Hudson Pl, Eldorado Pl, Hudson Blvd East, Luginsland (Carl Bitter). 50 ft, turned (rotation 60). 3 detected + 1 hand-picked.
streetnames: Park View Avenue or Duer Place

sheet-65.description: Sheet 65 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers the upland blocks of Weehawken between Bulls Ferry Road and Potter Place, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Bulls Ferry Road runs down the left edge with the Town of Union boundary line along it, and Fulton, Columbia Terrace, Clifton Terrace and Highwood Avenue or Liberty Place cross the sheet in four parallel rows, enclosing blocks 55, 52 and 51 and the strip of lots south of them. Block 55 and block 52 are lined with narrow lots; the houses are mostly two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings in yellow, with garages, and the sites of North Hudson Hospital (being built, in pink) and of a studio are marked. Block 51 holds the Park M.E. Church, the Old Park M.E. Church (not used) and the Norwegian Church, and at the left edge a group of brick flats with stores faces Bulls Ferry Road. Highwood Avenue branches off Liberty Place and runs diagonally to the lower right, past the Weehawken High School, a large pink brick building whose lettering describes its standpipes, hose, fire escapes and heating, and the line of Eldorado Place closes the lower right corner. A short street lettered F. St. enters block 50 from Liberty Place. The lower left, marked 63, and the lower right, marked 64, are drawn on other sheets, and sheet 67 lies above Fulton. Six inch water pipes, hydrants, a fire alarm box and a compass rose with a magnetic needle are shown.
notes: Fulton is printed without a suffix; today it is Fulton Street. Columbia Ter., Clifton Ter. and Potter Pl. are now Columbia Terrace, Clifton Terrace and Potter Place, and Highwood Av. or Liberty Pl. is Liberty Place.
Bulls Ferry Road along the left edge is Park Avenue on modern maps; the junctions used for control are on Park Avenue, which is mapped as two parallel carriageways in places.
Weehawken High School and the Park M.E. Church of 1910 are drawn here; North Hudson Hospital is marked as being built.
Fulton, Columbia Ter, Clifton Ter, Highwood Av or Liberty Pl, Potter Pl, Bulls Ferry Road. 50 ft.

sheet-66.description: Sheet 66 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers the blocks of upland Weehawken between Potter Place and Hudson Boulevard East, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Five parallel streets cross the sheet from the Potter Place side to the boulevard: Fulton at the top, then Columbia Terrace, Clifton Terrace, Liberty Place and Eldorado Place at the bottom, enclosing blocks 56, 53, 51 and 50. The blocks are divided into narrow lots running back from each street, and the houses are mostly two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings in yellow, with a few pink brick houses, rows of flats on Liberty Place and Eldorado Place, brick houses marked to be built, a cement block house, garages, and a house lettered Villa Norma on Columbia Terrace. At the end of Liberty Place near the boulevard stands a police sub-station with an office. Hudson Boulevard East curves along the right side of the blocks, its outer edge following the top of the Palisades; beyond it the sheet carries a flight of public steps, the note Bridge over Ravine and the margin note See Volume 8A, since the slope and river front are drawn in that volume. Louisa Place enters from the top, where a fire alarm box stands at its foot, and a short street lettered F. St. enters block 50 from Liberty Place at the left. The blank areas at the top, left, right and bottom carry the numbers of sheets 67, 65, 71 and 64. Six inch water pipes, hydrants and a compass rose with a magnetic needle are drawn in the streets.
notes: Fulton is printed without a suffix; today it is Fulton Street. Columbia Ter., Clifton Ter., Liberty Pl., Eldorado Pl. and Potter Pl. are Columbia Terrace, Clifton Terrace, Liberty Place, Eldorado Place and Potter Place; Hudson B'l'v'd East is Boulevard East.
Eight junctions detected along Potter Place and Boulevard East fit within about 1.4 m leave-one-out.
The Palisades slope east of Hudson Boulevard East is not drawn on this sheet and is carried in Volume 8A.
Fulton, Columbia Ter, Clifton Ter, Liberty Pl, Eldorado Pl, Potter Pl to Hudson Blvd East. 50 ft.

sheet-67.description: Sheet 67 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers three long blocks of upland Weehawken between Fulton and the cliff edge, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. Bulls Ferry Road crosses the top of the sheet on a diagonal, with the dash-dot boundary line between the Town of Union and Weehawken running down its middle, and Hudson Boulevard East curves along the bottom, beyond which the margin reads See Volume 8A. Fulton runs down the left edge, and 1st Street, 2nd Street and 3rd Street run parallel to it, dividing the sheet into blocks 57, 58 and 60; Louisa Place crosses near the bottom, with block 59 below it and the boulevard. The lots are narrow and deep, and nearly all carry two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings in yellow, with a few pink brick buildings and rows of flats. At the head of block 57, on Bulls Ferry Road, stand a plumber's works and three pink flats with sheds, a fire bell in a steel structure stands in the open ground near the boulevard end of 3rd Street, and the Grove Collegiate Church, drawn in blue, stands in block 59. At the lower right a row of brick and hollow-tile flats faces the boulevard, and Farley's Hotel with a saloon and shed stands beyond it at Clifton Road, noted as also shown on Volume 8A. The strip at the top right carries the street lettered Broadway, a compass rose, and a fire alarm box at the foot of 3rd Street. Sheets 65 and 66 lie to the left and sheet 68 to the right.
notes: Fulton is printed without a suffix; today it is Fulton Street. Louisa Pl. is now Louisa Place and Hudson Blvd East is Boulevard East.
1st, 2nd and 3rd Street were fitted to Cooper Place, 46th Street and 47th Street on modern maps (the control points sit at their junctions with Louisa Place and Boulevard East).
Bulls Ferry Road is Park Avenue on modern maps; its junctions along the top diagonal were not detected and are not used as control.
Farley's Hotel carries the note This Risk is also shown on Volume 8A.
Fulton, Louisa Pl, 1st-3rd St (Cooper Pl, 46th, 47th St), Bulls Ferry Road, Hudson Blvd East. 50 ft, turned (rotation 60). Bottom margin See Volume 8A.

sheet-68.description: Sheet 68 of the Hudson County volume 8 series covers the four blocks of Weehawken between Bulls Ferry Road and Hudson Boulevard East, from 3rd Street at the bottom to 7th Street at the top, where the West New York line runs along the top street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Bulls Ferry Road crosses the sheet on a slant at the left, with the dash-dot boundary line between West New York or the Town of Union and Weehawken down its middle, and Hudson Boulevard East bounds the blocks on the right with a curving edge along the Palisades. The blocks, numbered 1A, 2A, 62 and 61, are divided into narrow lots running between the streets. The houses are almost all two-and-a-half-storey frame dwellings in yellow, set in regular rows on 5th and 3rd Streets, with pink brick flats, stores and shops along Bulls Ferry Road, an office, a few brick flats near the boulevard on 6th Street, and several blocks of unbuilt lots, particularly on block 1A at the top. A small building near the boulevard on block 62 is coloured blue. The margins at the top and left read See Volume 8A, since the land beyond the West New York line and below the cliff is drawn in that volume, and a compass rose with a magnetic needle stands at the upper left. Sheet 67 lies below 3rd Street. Water pipes of 6 to 24 inches, hydrants, a fire alarm box and tap houses are drawn in the streets.
notes: 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th Street correspond to 47th to 51st Street on modern maps; the control points were fitted at their junctions with Boulevard East and with Park Avenue.
Bulls Ferry Road is Park Avenue on modern maps; Hudson Blvd East is Boulevard East.
The sheet lies along the West New York boundary: the streets beyond it (7th Street, 6th Street and others lettered at the left) are in West New York or Union and are drawn in Volume 8A.
3rd-7th St (now 47th-51st St), Bulls Ferry Road, Hudson Blvd East, West New York line. 50 ft.

sheet-69.description: Sheet 69 of the Hudson County volume 8 series, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, covers the Erie Railroad yards and piers on the Weehawken waterfront at the Hoboken line. Along the top runs Hudson Boulevard East (Park Avenue), with Branch Road above it, from the viaduct approach and 19th Street at the left past a row of dwellings and stores to the Erie Railroad Company's cattle pens, which fill the upper right with numbered pen blocks, scales, an open platform and a dilapidated section. Below lie the old round house used for storage, the New Jersey Junction Railroad and the broad fan of tracks of the Erie Railroad yards, with storage sheds of the O'Rourke Engineering and Construction Company. The lower half of the sheet shows the Erie Railroad Company's marine yard with its repair shop, marine railway and oil storage at the left, and the Erie piers lettered D to J reaching into the Hudson River: some carry tracks on piles, two have long freight sheds of the Erie Railroad, and one is a coal trestle. The Weehawken and Hoboken boundary line crosses the lower left corner diagonally, and the pier and bulkhead lines approved by the Secretary of War in 1897 are drawn across the river. A general report on the yards' watchmen, fire alarm system and hose is printed at lower right, and the left margin is marked to see Volume Seven.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East (Park Avenue) here is today's Park Avenue, south of its junction with Boulevard East.
The Erie yards, cattle pens and piers are gone; the area is now Lincoln Harbor.

Placed from the single junction 19th Street / Park Avenue with the 100 ft scale and a rotation of 58 degrees chosen to fit the buildings shared with sheet 58 and the pier sequence of sheet 70; low confidence on the piers.

Erie R.R. yards and piers D to J, Hudson Blvd East (Park Av), Branch Road, 19th St, cattle pens. 100 ft. Anchored on 19th St / Park Av (detector position, entered by hand) with north 58 degrees, which the ties to sheets 58 and 70 support (the measured lines gave 62 and left a 50 to 75 m gap to sheet 70). Low confidence on the piers.

sheet-70.description: Sheet 70 of the Hudson County volume 8 series, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north towards the upper right, continues the Weehawken waterfront north of sheet 69. Hudson Boulevard East curves across the top below Branch Road, and Baldwin Avenue (Coaldock Road) runs down from it to the shore past the Erie Railroad Company's cattle pens, the James Emslie Horse Company's export stable and the Pennsylvania Railroad tunnel pit, walled in concrete, with the office and engine room of the O'Rourke Engineering and Construction Company, contractors for the tunnel. A stone crusher plant and its incline stand east of Baldwin Avenue. Across the middle run the tracks of the Erie Railroad yards and the New Jersey Junction Railroad right of way. Below them are the Erie Railroad warehouse Annex C on piles, three Erie Railroad pier sheds on piers A to C and a freight car bridge at the left, and the Delaware and Hudson Canal Company's basin, buildings and coal trestles, marked not used, at the right, with the floating dry dock of a dry dock company at the right edge. Most of the right half above the tracks is open ground below the cliff. The exterior lines for solid filling and for piers approved by the Secretary of War in 1897 are drawn across the Hudson River at the bottom.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East is now Boulevard East; Baldwin Avenue keeps its name.
The Pennsylvania Railroad tunnel pit is the Weehawken shaft of the North River tunnels, under construction in 1910.

Placed from two building corners by the New Jersey Junction Railroad carried from sheet 71, with the 100 ft scale and a rotation of 57.5 degrees; the modern Baldwin Avenue / Boulevard East node lies about 100 m from the 1910 junction and was not used. Low confidence.

Erie R.R. yards, piers A to C, Delaware & Hudson Canal Co, Baldwin Av (Coal Dock Road), Hudson Blvd East, Penna R.R. tunnel pit. 100 ft. Anchored on two building corners carried from sheet 71, north 57.5. The earlier hand pick at the modern Baldwin Av / Boulevard East node put it about 100 m east of where sheet 57 draws that junction; the modern node does not match the 1910 junction. Its Baldwin Av corner still lies about 38 m from sheet 57's placement of it. Low confidence.

sheet-71.description: Sheet 71 of the Hudson County volume 8 series, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the foot of the Palisades and the Hudson River shore in Weehawken between Clifton Road and the Delaware and Hudson basin. Only a strip along the left edge is built up: Hudson Boulevard East runs along the top of the cliff past Eldorado Place, Hudson Place and Duer Place, with a few large houses on its east side, and turns west at Hamilton Avenue, which continues south past Bellevue Street. Below the cliff the tracks of the New Jersey Junction Railroad run the length of the sheet next to the curving shore line. At the top, along Clifton Road and the iron bridge with its plank floor, are the Clifton House, the West Shore Railroad and the Union Dry Dock and Repair Company with two floating dry docks and an old dry dock used for storage. The rest of the sheet is open water, crossed by the dashed exterior lines for solid filling and for piers, the latter approved by the Secretary of War in 1897; the top margin refers to Volume 8A.
notes: Hudson Boulevard East is now Boulevard East.

The shore and dry docks lie under later fill (Port Imperial); the sheet is placed from eight points carried from sheets 62 and 64 (junctions and block corners along the boulevard and at the turn of Hamilton Avenue), all at its left edge, so the river side is extrapolated.

Waterfront below the cliff: New Jersey Junction R.R., Union Dry Dock, Hamilton Av, Hudson Blvd East, Duer Pl, Hudson Pl. 100 ft. Placed from 8 points carried from sheets 64 and 62 along its left edge; the river side is extrapolated.

sheet-72.description: Sheet 72 of the Hudson County volume 8 series, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers a thinly built tract on the Palisades in Weehawken between Hudson Boulevard East and the New Jersey Junction Railroad. Hudson Boulevard East, 80 feet wide, sweeps down the left side of the sheet in a long S curve along the edge of the cliff. In the upper middle, High Bluff Terrace, a 40 foot street, comes down from sheet 62, turns east along a row of lots and then winds south through a laid-out subdivision of narrow lots, block 36, of which only two houses are built: a frame dwelling and a stone dwelling with frame additions. The right side of the sheet is the right of way of the New Jersey Junction Railroad with its tracks along the right edge, and the large open area between the boulevard and the railroad is left blank. The margins give the numbers of the adjoining sheets 57, 59, 60, 62, 70 and 71.
notes: High Bluff Terrace does not survive in the modern street network.
Placed from two corners carried from sheet 62 (High Bluff Terrace at the lot line on the shared edge) and a point derived from them; scale from the atlas, low confidence.
High Bluff Terrace and Hudson Blvd East on the cliff, New Jersey Junction R.R. right of way. 50 ft.
